name: Archaic Finnish Swedish / de östsvenska dialekterna
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Vendell, Herman. 1904. Ordbok över de östsvenska dialekterna, h. 1 (Skrifter utgivna av Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland 64). Helsingfors: Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland. Inledning, Kap. III 'Aksent', §§ 40–41, pp. XXV–XXVI. Corroborated by Vendell 1892 Pedersöre-Purmo-målet § 14 pp. 196–198; Freudenthal 1889 Vöråmålet § 96 p. 42; Freudenthal 1878 Ueber den Närpesdialect § 33 pp. 57–58.
catalog_locator: Inledning, Kap. III 'Aksent', § 40, pp. XXV–XXVI (pp. 31–32 of the archive.org copy ordbokverdestsv00vendgoog)
catalog_quote: Kap. III. Aksent. § 40. Den exspiratoriska huvudaksenten hvilar i allmänhet på ordets första betonade stavelse utom i vNyl, där dels semifortis övergått till fortis dels andra för nsv. riksspråket främmande tonlägen påträffas (se min nyss citerade avh.); därmed överensstämmer i viss mån uttalet i Hitis, som bl. a. uppvisar stark levis efter acc. medius eller compositus — något, som också är fallet i Ålands härads folkmål. Å olika trakter, troligen mest i Österbotten, kvarstår allt än tvåspetsig fortis på kvantitatift långa enstaviga ord. Då således i avseende å exsp. aks. stor olikhet råder mellan dialekterna, har det varit ogörligt att utmärka dess läge i andra fall än sådana, [XXVI] då fortis hvilar på annan stavelse än i nhsv. (som t. ex. när i östb. fortis ligger på första stavelsen, ehuru denna är kort men ultima l. penultima långvokalisk, ss. till dömes ntr. sbst. på -i och verb på -er[a]). Fortis' läge angives då med ˈ.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: § 40. Den exspiratoriska huvudaksenten hvilar i allmänhet på ordets första betonade stavelse utom i vNyl, där dels semifortis övergått till fortis dels andra för nsv. riksspråket främmande tonlägen påträffas (se min nyss citerade avh.); därmed överensstämmer i viss mån uttalet i Hitis, som bl. a. uppvisar stark levis efter acc. medius eller compositus — något, som också är fallet i Ålands härads folkmål. ... har det varit ogörligt att utmärka dess läge i andra fall än sådana, då fortis hvilar på annan stavelse än i nhsv. (som t. ex. när i östb. fortis ligger på första stavelsen, ehuru denna är kort men ultima l. penultima långvokalisk ...). Fortis' läge angives då med ˈ.
new_statements.translation: § 40. The expiratory main accent rests in general on the word's first stressed [stressable] syllable, except in West Nyland, where partly semifortis has become fortis and partly other pitch patterns foreign to the modern Swedish standard language occur (see my treatise just cited); the pronunciation in Hitis agrees with this to some extent, showing i.a. a strong levis after accentus medius or compositus — something that is also the case in the folk dialects of Ålands härad. ... it has been impossible to mark its position except in cases where fortis rests on a different syllable than in modern High Swedish (as e.g. when in Ostrobothnian fortis lies on the first syllable although it is short and the ultima or penultima has a long vowel ...). The position of fortis is then indicated with ˈ.
new_statements.citation: Vendell, Herman. 1904. Ordbok över de östsvenska dialekterna, h. 1 (Skrifter utgivna av Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland 64). Helsingfors: Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland.

Aksent. § 40. Den exspiratoriska huvudaksenten hvilar i allmänhet på ordets första betonade stavelse utom i vNyl, där dels semifortis övergått till fortis dels andra för nsv. riksspråket främmande tonlägen påträffas (se min nyss citerade avh.); därmed överensstämmer i viss mån uttalet i Hitis, som bl. a. uppvisar stark levis efter acc. medius eller compositus — något, som också är fallet i Ålands härads folkmål. Å olika trakter, troligen mest i Österbotten, kvarstår allt än tvåspetsig fortis på kvantitatift långa enstaviga ord. Då således…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary (expiratory) stress falls as a rule on the first syllable of the word (Germanic root-initial stress) across the Swedish folk dialects of Finland; Ostrobothnian dialects extend initial stress even to foreign loanwords that have non-initial stress in Standard Swedish (Närpes prédik, húser — Freudenthal 1878:57; Vörå 'vanligen.. på ordets första stafvelse' — Freudenthal 1889:42; Karleby–Nedervetil ˈkosin, ˈmosik, ˈridzir — Ivars 2015:89–90; Pedersöre-Purmo 'i allmänhet på första stafvelsen' but many loans keep original stress, aféd, kaplán, musík — Vendell 1892:196), while Åland has 'den för svenskan normala rörliga betoningen' (ˈströmming but akˈsjo:n, hisˈtorja — Ivars 2015:179). In compounds main stress is normally on the first member.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Vendell 1892 § 14.2 (Pedersöre-Purmo): strong secondary stress ('stark biton') on the first syllable of trisyllables whose final syllable carries main stress (brìŋgarí) and on the first syllable — if long or closed — of the second member of a compound (bǻtstàm); weak secondary stress on the second syllable of an initially-stressed disyllable (túlù 'tålig') and on the third syllable of initially-stressed tri/polysyllables; any syllable between two stressed ones is unstressed. Ivars 2015:179 (Åland): 'huvudbetoningen normalt på det första sammansättningsledet och bibetoningen på det senare'. Vendell 1904 § 40: in West Nyland, Hitis and Ålands härad the compound secondary (semifortis/levis) is strengthened, up to fortis in West Nyland.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed prefixes be-, för-, o-, te- (Vendell 1892 § 14.3); loanwords with non-initial stress, regionally variable (kept in Pedersöre aféd, agúst, kaplán, matrós, semendrú; kept in Åland akˈsjo:n, perˈfekt, tje:naˈrinnår; recent loans in Närpes ambuláns, biljétt, direktö́r — Ivars 1988:215; but pulled to the first syllable in Närpes/Vörå/Karleby older loans); Freudenthal 1889 notes 'icke få undantag' marked individually in his glossary; compounds with main stress on the second member (Pedersöre kaprét, kolstímand, merkvéd, obárt; W Åland lammˈungar, moˈrötter; Brändö place-names Nårrˈgrinnån); name groups take phrase stress on the last element (Pell ˈA:gust); West Nyland 'upptaktsbetoning' in compounds and foreign trisyllables (Selenius 1972 ch. 8); monosyllabic function words lose stress by sentence position (Freudenthal 1889 § 10.11).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level expiratory ('dynamic') accent as marked in dictionary/glossary citation forms (Vendell marks fortis with ˈ only where it deviates from Standard Swedish; Freudenthal 1889 marks exceptions in the Ordlista). Tonal word accent is a separate dimension: most of the area has only accent 1 (no acc.1/acc.2 contrast) — West Nyland and Eckerö (W Åland) keep the contrast; Närpes/Solf/Kimito show non-distinctive grave-like contours (Ivars 2015:82–83, 179, 228, 280).
new_statements.identity_note: Vendell's 'östsvenska dialekterna' covers ALL Swedish folk dialects east of the Baltic: Finland (Österbotten, Åland, Åboland/Egentliga Finland, Nyland = Glottolog east2303) plus the 'baltiska mål' of Estonia and Gammalsvenskby (= esto1259). § 40 is stated for the whole area, with West Nyland (vNyl), Hitis and Ålands härad flagged as deviating (secondary stress promoted, 'upptaktsbetoning'). Corroborating first-hand statements are parish-level: Freudenthal 1878 = Närpes (S Österbotten), Freudenthal 1889 = Vörå (C Österbotten), Vendell 1892 = Pedersöre-Purmo (N Österbotten); Ivars 2015 gives regional statements (Karleby–Nedervetil initial stress incl. loanwords; Åland 'movable stress as in Swedish'). The languoid is internally heterogeneous: Ostrobothnian dialects pull loanwords to initial stress (Finnish contact), Åland/West Nyland behave like Uppland Swedish. Hultman 1939:84 cautions that Vendell's accent notes in this very introduction are 'delvis högst dubiösa' (context: syllable/tonal accent, not stress locus).

tone_statements.citation: [Chapter 2, author not named in the Crossref record]. 2009 [Crossref: 2010]. Prosodic features of compound words in some Southwestern dialects of Swedish in Finland. In: Vainio, Martti, Reijo Aulanko & Olli Aaltonen (eds.), Nordic Prosody: Proceedings of the Xth Conference, Helsinki 2008, pp. 19 ff. Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang.
tone_statements.quote: Accent och intonation De östnyländska dialekterna saknar oppositionen mellan Accent 1 och Accent 2. Ordaccentoppositionen verkar ha levt kvar i många delar av Finland ända till 1900-talet, men i östnyländskan tycks den ha försvunnit för rätt längre sedan (Vendell 1897). Aho (denna volym) har en närmare diskussion av accent och intonation.
tone_statements.translation: Accent and intonation. The East Nyland dialects lack the opposition between Accent 1 and Accent 2. The word-accent opposition seems to have survived in many parts of Finland right up to the 20th century, but in East Nyland speech it appears to have disappeared rather long ago (Vendell 1897). Aho (this volume) has a closer discussion of accent and intonation.
tone_statements.summary: East Nyland Swedish incl. Liljendal: no Accent 1 ~ Accent 2 word-accent contrast, lost long ago (citing Vendell 1897); author adds it survived elsewhere in Finland into the 1900s; details left to Aho.

tone_statements.citation: Aho, Eija. 2008. Om prosodin i Liljendaldialekten. In: Palmén, Helena, Caroline Sandström & Jan-Ola Östman (eds.), Dialekt i östra Nyland: Fältarbete i Liljendal med omnejd (Nordica Helsingiensia 14; Dialektforskning 1), 39–52 [37–52 in Ivars 2015]. Helsingfors: Nordica, Helsingfors universitet.
tone_statements.quote: Även i de tvåstaviga orden kan man se en tydlig tendens mot preferens för stigande intonation i den betonade vokalen medan fallande intonation är tämligen icke-frekvent. ... Utifrån det analyserade materialet verkar det inte finnas någon accentdistribution i dialekten, vilket är kännetecknande för finlandssvenskan (se avsnitt 2.4.4). Materialet i denna studie är dock för litet för att kunna dra några vidare slutsatser om detta.
tone_statements.translation: In the disyllabic words too one can see a clear tendency towards a preference for rising intonation in the stressed vowel, while falling intonation is fairly infrequent. ... On the basis of the analysed material there seems to be no accent distribution [i.e. no acute/grave word-accent distinction] in the dialect, which is characteristic of Finland Swedish (see section 2.4.4). The material in this study is, however, too small to draw any further conclusions about this.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 66-67, section 4.3.2 'Intonation i betonade en- och tvåstaviga ord i fritt tal', last paragraphs
tone_statements.summary: Praat F0 study (60 stressed words, 5 speakers): no acute/grave word-accent distinction found, stated tentatively (material small); stressed vowels mostly show a late rising F0 peak.

tone_statements.citation: Kim, Yuni. 2006. Variation and Finnish influence in Finland Swedish dialect intonation. Working Papers (Lund University, Dept. of Linguistics and Phonetics) 52 (Proceedings of Fonetik 2006): 77–80.
tone_statements.quote: Dialekterna i östra Åboland har olika typer av ordaccenter som används osystematiskt. Även tvåtoppiga accenter förekommer då och då men ingen betydelseskiljande accent har bevarats. ... Dialekten i Nagu påminner prosodiskt mera om sverigesvenskan än om finlandssvenskt standardspråk. Den tvåtoppiga ordaccenten är mycket vanlig även om det antagligen inte mera finns ett betydelseskiljande accentsystem såsom i västra Nyland och i delar av Åland (Selenius 1972 och 1978; Harling-Kranck 1998). Vi såg dock ett exempel från Nagu där en betydelseskiljande accent eller betydelseskiljande betoning upprätthålls.
tone_statements.translation: The dialects of eastern Åboland have different types of word accents that are used unsystematically. Two-peaked accents also occur now and then, but no meaning-distinguishing accent has been preserved. ... The Nagu dialect is prosodically more reminiscent of Sweden Swedish than of Finland-Swedish standard language. The two-peaked word accent is very common, although there probably no longer is a meaning-distinguishing accent system as in western Nyland and parts of Åland (Selenius 1972 and 1978; Harling-Kranck 1998). We did, however, see one example from Nagu where a meaning-distinguishing accent or meaning-distinguishing stress is maintained.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 30-31, section 'Sammanfattning och diskussion'; cf. p. 17 for the same statement on Kimito/Pargas/Västanfjärd
tone_statements.summary: F0 study: one- and two-peaked phonetic accents occur, but no distinctive word accent survives in E. Aboland; Nagu probably none either, though the author leaves it open (paron pear/potato, p. 20).

tone_statements.citation: Svärd, Nina. 2001. Word accents in the Närpes dialect: Is there really only one accent? Working Papers (Lund University, Dept. of Linguistics) 49 (Proceedings of Fonetik 2001): 160–163.
tone_statements.quote: § 9. Musikalisk akcent. Med hänsyn till formen är den musikaliska akcenten likaledes av två slag: enkel ock sammansatt. Om den musikaliska akcentens höjd på tonskalan kan jag för tillfället ej lemna närmare upplysning. Den huvudtoniga stavelsen torde dock ha den musikaliskt högsta tonen, den bitoniga en lägre, den obetonade den lägsta. Intervallerna torde ej vara stora. ... 2. Akcent cirkumflex (sammansatt akcent) förekommer utpräglad endast då två stavelser sammansmälta till en ... Mindre utpräglad är cirkumflexen i sammandragna ord ... Anm. 3. Emedan målets akcentuationssystem är så enkelt, lemnas akcenten obetecknad i det följande.
tone_statements.translation: § 9. Musical accent. As to form the musical accent is likewise of two kinds: simple and compound. On the height of the musical accent on the tonal scale I cannot at present give closer information. The main-stressed syllable should however have the musically highest tone, the secondary-stressed a lower one, the unstressed the lowest. The intervals are probably not large. ... 2. Circumflex accent (compound accent) occurs in marked form only when two syllables merge into one ... Less marked is the circumflex in contracted words ... Note 3. Since the dialect's accentuation system is so simple, accent is left unmarked in what follows.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Musical accent simple vs compound (circumflex), the latter only in syllables contracted from two; pitch height follows stress grade; judged by ear; accent left unmarked as 'so simple'.

tone_statements.citation: Selenius, Ebba. 1984. Pargas med akut och Pargas med grav. In: Festskrift till Åke Granlund 28.4.1984 (Studier i nordisk filologi 65; Skrifter utgivna av Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland 517), 223–228. Helsingfors: Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland.
tone_statements.quote: A basic division is into single-peaked (Far East, South, Central) and double-peaked dialect types (East, West). Among the singlepeaked dialects Far East (Finland) Swedish is singled out by its absence of the word accent distinction. ... Even for dialects of Far East (Finland) Swedish that do not have the word accent distinction it seems to be meaningful to apply this categorization. Thus if we assume the pitch accent gesture of such a dialect type to be comparable to the accent I pattern of another dialect having the word accent distinction, dialects of Far East Swedish can be included in this categorization.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2 Background; sec. 4.3 Word accentuation; cf. Table 1, column 'word accent contrast' = no for Far East S and Far East N (proceedings pp. 175-178 per the ISCA archive record)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Finland Swedish dialects lack the accent I/II tonal contrast; one pitch gesture treated like accent I, timed late (S Finland) vs early (East Botnia). Credited to Garding, confirmed on SweDia data.

sources.note: § 40: expiratory main accent 'i allmänhet på ordets första betonade stavelse' throughout the East Swedish dialects, except West Nyland (semifortis > fortis, foreign 'tonlägen'), partly Hitis and Ålands härad (strong levis after acc. medius/compositus); fortis marked in entries only where it differs from Standard Swedish (e.g. Ostrobothnian fortis on a short first syllable before long-vowel ultima). § 41: accent 2 lacking in all Baltic (Estonian) dialects, central Nyland from Sjundeå eastward, East Nyland, Pargas, Gamlakarleby, Nedervetil; both tonal accents elsewhere.

sources.note: Per-region 'Prosodiska egenskaper' sections treat mainly tonal accent (only West Nyland and Eckerö/W Åland keep the acc.1/acc.2 contrast; elsewhere one accent, '0-type') and quantity. Stress locus: Karleby–Nedervetil p. 89–90 'Det är ett för dialekten typiskt mönster att betoningen ligger på första stavelsen och att andra stavelsen förkortas, t.ex. ˈridzir 'regera'.. ˈmosik' (French loans, Finnish contact); Åland p. 179 'I flerstaviga enkla ord kan betoningens plats variera.. ˈströmming.. men akˈsjo:n, förˈäldrar, hisˈtorja.. Huvudmönstret är således den för svenskan normala rörliga betoninge…

sources.citation: Ivars, Ann-Marie. 1988. Närpesdialekten på 1980-talet (Studier i nordisk filologi 70; SSLS 552). Helsingfors: SLS. 280 pp.
sources.note: Explicitly excludes prosody: 'Att satsmelodin och de prosodiska dragen hos dialekten (dvs. satsintonation, betoning, accent) inte kommit med i den här presentationen beror.. på att de utgör ett mycket svårt och tidskrävande forskningsområde'. Incidental: compound examples 'alla med betoningen på första stavelsen (békåli osv.)'; new loan nouns 'med betoningen på sista stavelsen' (ambulans, biljett, direktör..) p. 215.

sources.citation: Selenius, Ebba. 1972. Västnyländsk ordaccent (Studier i nordisk filologi 59; SSLS 451). Helsingfors: SLS. 298 pp.
sources.note: Instrumental/auditory monograph on West Nyland (Snappertuna etc.) tonal word accent; ch. 8 'Upptaktsbetoning i västra Nyland' pp. 199–220 documents non-initial (second-member/final) stress in compounds and foreign trisyllables (rule p. c. 125: one intervocalic consonant -> upptaktsbetoning as in Standard Swedish, kavéra; cluster -> grave accent, stressed like a compound); notes p. 106 that many Swedish dialects put main stress on the first syllable of foreign trisyllables.

sources.citation: Hultman, O. F. 1939. Efterlämnade skrifter II: Föreläsningar över de östsvenska dialekterna, utg. av Rolf Pipping och Olav Ahlbäck (Skrifter utg. av SLS 274). Helsingfors. 306 pp.
sources.note: Historical vowel/consonant developments by 'starktonig/svagtonig stafvelse'; no synchronic stress-locus rule. p. 84: knowledge of East Swedish accent is incomplete, Vendell's accent notes in the Ordbok introduction 'delvis högst dubiösa'; E Finland Proper and central/east Nyland dialects 'ha antagit det finska aksentsystemet' (acute syllable accent, strongly falling expiratory pressure), West Nyland keeps old Swedish accentuation.

sources.note: '§ 14. För den exspiratoriska aksenten gälla följande regler: 1) Hufvudtonen hvilar a) i enkla ord: i allmänhet på första stafvelsen, dock ingalunda i så stort omfång som i Kronoby- och Gamlakarleby-målen' (loanwords keep original fortis: aféd, agúst, kaplán, matrós, musík.; third syllable in semendrú 'seminarium'); b) compounds: on the first member's first tone-syllable (lédudör), exceptions with stress on 2nd member (kaprét, kolstímand, merkvéd, obárt); 2) strong secondary stress on 1st syllable of trisyllables with final main stress and on the (long/closed) 1st syllable of a 2nd compound m…

sources.citation: Freudenthal, A. O. 1889. Vöråmålet: ljud- och formlära, ordlista med register, språkprof. Helsingfors: Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland. § 96 'Aksent', p. 42.
sources.note: '.. att målet i likhet med flertalet andra östsvenska dialekter äger gravis, att cirkumflex på rotstafvelsen ersätter slutvokalens bortfall i ursprungligen tvåstafviga ord, om rotvokalen är lång, och att, hvad tonvikten beträffar, denna vanligen med största styrka faller på ordets första stafvelse. Som emellertid icke få undantag från denna regel finnas, har jag i Ordlistan med ˈ utmärkt läget för den exspiratoriska hufvudaksenten.' Also § 10.11: monosyllables från/få/slå/på lose stress by sentence position.

sources.note: Musical accent of Närpes (and most Swedish folk dialects of Finland) has gravis like Sweden Swedish, unlike educated Finland Swedish; 'Auch im exspiratorischen Accent oder der Betonung unterscheidet sich die Närpesmundart von der Sprache der Gebildeten, da derselbe auch in ausländischen Lehnwörtern auf der ersten Sylbe ruht, vergl. z. B. schw. predika.. und np. prédik, schw. husera.. und np. húser.'

sources.citation: Aho, Eija. 2010. Spontaanin puheen prosodinen jaksottelu. PhD diss., Helsingin yliopisto (includes Aho 2010a on tonal features of Ostrobothnian, Åboland and Nyland dialects and Aho 2010b on Solf).
sources.note: Only modern instrumental prosodic study spanning several east2303 dialect regions; would confirm stress locus and refine the regional split (Finnish-like vs Sweden-like prosody) that Ivars 2015 reports from it.

sources.note: The Glottolog-cited source: a comparative historical sound-law survey organised by dialect group (Nyland, Eg. Finland, Åland, Österbotten, Satakunda, Estonia); refers throughout to hufvudtonig/svagtonig/bitonig syllables and 'satsaksent' but gives no rule for the position of word stress (a full-text search for stress/accent aksent/hufvudton/betoning read in context).

sources.citation: Freudenthal, A. O. 1870. Om svenska allmogemålet i Nyland (Bidrag till kännedom af Finlands natur och folk 15). Helsingfors: Finska Vetenskaps-Societeten. Inledning pp. 9–10.
sources.note: 'betoningen eller tonfallet': educated Finland Swedish lacks the low tone (accentus gravis); most folk dialects (Österbotten, Åland, Egentliga Finland) have it; Nyland splits into western Raseborg (has gravis) vs the rest (always high tone, like 'finsk brytning' and Estonian Swedish). No statement on stress position.

tone.quote: Accent och intonation De östnyländska dialekterna saknar oppositionen mellan Accent 1 och Accent 2. Ordaccentoppositionen verkar ha levt kvar i många delar av Finland ända till 1900-talet, men i östnyländskan tycks den ha försvunnit för rätt längre sedan (Vendell 1897). Aho (denna volym) har en närmare diskussion av accent och intonation.
tone.translation: Accent and intonation. The East Nyland dialects lack the opposition between Accent 1 and Accent 2. The word-accent opposition seems to have survived in many parts of Finland right up to the 20th century, but in East Nyland speech it appears to have disappeared rather long ago (Vendell 1897). Aho (this volume) has a closer discussion of accent and intonation.

tone.translation: In the disyllabic words too one can see a clear tendency towards a preference for rising intonation in the stressed vowel, while falling intonation is fairly infrequent. ... On the basis of the analysed material there seems to be no accent distribution [i.e. no acute/grave word-accent distinction] in the dialect, which is characteristic of Finland Swedish (see section 2.4.4). The material in this study is, however, too small to draw any further conclusions about this.

tone.translation: The dialects of eastern Åboland have different types of word accents that are used unsystematically. Two-peaked accents also occur now and then, but no meaning-distinguishing accent has been preserved. ... The Nagu dialect is prosodically more reminiscent of Sweden Swedish than of Finland-Swedish standard language. The two-peaked word accent is very common, although there probably no longer is a meaning-distinguishing accent system as in western Nyland and parts of Åland (Selenius 1972 and 1978; Harling-Kranck 1998). We did, however, see one example from Nagu where a meaning-distinguishing accent or meaning-distinguishing stress is maintained.

tone.translation: § 9. Musical accent. As to form the musical accent is likewise of two kinds: simple and compound. On the height of the musical accent on the tonal scale I cannot at present give closer information. The main-stressed syllable should however have the musically highest tone, the secondary-stressed a lower one, the unstressed the lowest. The intervals are probably not large. ... 2. Circumflex accent (compound accent) occurs in marked form only when two syllables merge into one ... Less marked is the circumflex in contracted words ... Note 3. Since the dialect's accentuation system is so simple, accent is left unmarked in what follows.

sources.quote: A basic division is into single-peaked (Far East, South, Central) and double-peaked dialect types (East, West). Among the singlepeaked dialects Far East (Finland) Swedish is singled out by its absence of the word accent distinction. ... Even for dialects of Far East (Finland) Swedish that do not have the word accent distinction it seems to be meaningful to apply this categorization. Thus if we assume the pitch accent gesture of such a dialect type to be comparable to the accent I pattern of another dialect having the word accent distinction, dialects of Far East Swedish can be included in this categorization.

tone.quote: It is a commonly held assumption that the acute/grave distinction is not manifested in most Finland-Swedish dialects and that the acute accent is generalized. ... The results suggest that the tonal pattern in words, which receive acute accent in Standard Swedish, differ from that in words which receive grave accent in a systematic way. ... It is suggested that a weakening of the acoustic correlates of the accent distinction has led to the loss of the phonological distinction but without a complete loss of the patterns that were once used distinctively. ... It thus seems that the accent realisations only have one peak, with the grave peak occurring earlier in the word than the acute peak.

tone.quote: Orden återges precis som jag vid tillfället hört och uppfattat dem. Ord som antecknats förledsaccentuerade, ha stundom bitryck utsatt på efterleden. Förledens accentform kan vara gravis eller akut. I ord med efterledsaccent har ibland bitryck utsatts på förleden, ibland har grav accentform angivits på förleden men efterledens övervikt uttryckts med dubbla accenttecken. Ord, i vilka jämn accent, såväl på förleden som på efterleden antecknats, ha räknats dubbelt och upptagits såväl i grupp I som i grupp II.
tone.translation: The words are reproduced exactly as I heard and perceived them on the occasion. Words noted as first-member-accented sometimes have secondary stress marked on the second member. The accent form of the first member can be grave or acute. In words with second-member accent, secondary stress has sometimes been marked on the first member; sometimes grave accent form has been indicated on the first member but the predominance of the second member expressed with double accent signs. Words in which even accent, on the first as well as the second member, was noted have been counted twice and entered in both group I and group II.
